# RFC-0007: Interactive editing and provenance

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @wael
> **Tags:** `architecture`, `out-of-core`, `gui`

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0007:C-OVERVIEW] Overview and scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0007c-overview"></a>

Manual correction — lasso a region and reclassify, delete strays, fix ground the classifier got wrong — is
the greater part of what a point cloud workbench is used for, and the thing an immutable lazy pipeline
appears unable to express. This RFC specifies how it is expressed anyway.

**Scope** — how an edit is represented and stored; how the document reaches the screen and what is
invalidated when it changes; how a long edit stack is consolidated; and what record is kept of what was
changed.

**Out of scope** — the operator contract an edit is evaluated under ([RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md)). Point references, which
the enumerated edit form depends on ([RFC-0005:C-IDENTITY](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-identity)). What the renderer draws into
([RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md)). Selection interaction and tool ergonomics.

Two moves carry most of the weight. An edit stores **the gesture, not the points** — a lasso over forty
thousand points is a polygon, a predicate and an action, about a kilobyte regardless of reach, needing no
point identity at all. And the renderer consumes a **derived snapshot** refreshed at one one-way
synchronisation point, which is what lets it show an edit immediately without traversing the operator planner
and so without breaching [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) 1.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0007:C-EDIT] Edit representation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-edit"></a>

An edit is stored as the gesture that produced it. This keeps an edit's size independent of its reach, makes
it re-evaluable rather than baked, and — for the ordinary case — removes any need for per-point identity,
which the source formats cannot supply.

1. An edit MUST be a node in the document graph, evaluated as an ordinary operator subject to
   [RFC-0002:C-EXEC](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-exec) and [RFC-0002:C-MEMORY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-memory).
2. The default form is a **region edit**: a spatial region, an optional attribute predicate, and an action.
   - Its stored size MUST be independent of the number of points it affects.
   - It MUST be expressible as a spatial query against a source's index, so that evaluating it touches only
     the partitions its region intersects.
3. A **point-set edit**, which enumerates the points it affects, MAY be provided for corrections no region
   can express.
   - It MUST declare a maximum number of points it may enumerate, and MUST refuse a selection exceeding it.
   - That maximum MUST be reported to the user when a selection is refused.
   - Its references and permitted graph position are governed by [RFC-0005:C-IDENTITY](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-identity).
4. The edit stack is an **ordered sequence**, not a set. Reordering two edits MUST be treated as changing the
   result.
   - Reordering MAY be treated as result-preserving only where the system applies a stated independence
     test, and that test MUST be recorded with the reordering.
5. An edit MUST NOT modify a source. Sources are read-only, and the edited state exists only as the document
   graph applied to them.

#### Rationale

(2) is the whole economy of the design. A polygon of fifty vertices describes a selection of any size; it
survives reprojection and resampling, where a list of point references would not; and because it is a
spatial predicate it composes with the octree index rather than fighting it — editing is spatially sparse,
and the index already exists to find sparse regions.

(3) exists because the region form has a real gap: deselecting twelve stray returns among their neighbours is
an enumeration, and no region tight enough to isolate them is meaningfully a region. Requiring the bound to
be *declared and reported* rather than merely to exist is what makes the escape hatch checkable — an
unstated bound is unfalsifiable, and the bound is what keeps the enumerated form from quietly becoming the
default.

(4)'s nested carve-out replaces an earlier "unless the system can demonstrate independence", which was
unfalsifiable: any implementation could assert it had demonstrated something. Requiring a *stated* test that
is *recorded* makes the claim auditable, and keeps reordering available where it is genuinely safe — two
edits over disjoint regions with disjoint predicates commute, and that is worth being able to use.

(5) is what makes the whole model non-destructive: the original survives every edit, so no edit sequence can
lose data, and a remote source needs no write access.

### [RFC-0007:C-EXTRACT] Document authority and the render boundary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-extract"></a>

The renderer must show an edit the instant it is made, yet [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) 1 forbids the render path
from traversing the operator planner. Both hold if the renderer consumes a *derived snapshot* rather than the
document itself, refreshed at one defined synchronisation point.

1. The document graph is the sole authority for what the data is.
   - Any render-side representation MUST be derived from it, and MUST NOT be authoritative for any purpose.
2. Data MUST flow from document to render state in one direction only.
   - A render-side representation MUST NOT write back to the document graph.
3. There MUST be exactly one synchronisation point — the **extract** — at which the document graph and render
   state are both accessed.
   - The render path MUST NOT traverse the document graph outside it.
4. Extract MUST operate on metadata alone: which partitions are visible, and which edits apply to each.
   - It MUST NOT read point data.
   - It MUST NOT perform retrieval, and MUST NOT await it.

#### Rationale

(1) and (2) are what stop the renderer's compromises becoming the document's. The render path works at a
reduced level of detail by design; if that representation could write back, a camera position would be able
to change results. One-way flow makes that structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

(4) is the requirement most easily lost, and losing it stalls every frame. Where a system's authoritative
state is resident in memory, extraction copies values cheaply. Here the point data is not resident, so
extract must copy *plans* — partition references and edit sets — with the points arriving asynchronously
afterwards. An extract that awaited retrieval would put I/O inside the synchronisation point, which is the
one place nothing may block.

### [RFC-0007:C-INVALIDATION] Incremental invalidation of render state (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-invalidation"></a>

Rebuilding render state each frame is what a general-purpose engine does, and here it would mean
re-uploading a viewport of points every frame — precisely the cost this project exists to avoid. Retaining it
means invalidating only what changed, which only works if "what changed" is cheap to determine.

1. Render state MUST be retained across frames rather than rebuilt.
   - Retention is subject to eviction under memory pressure and to partitions leaving the view; this item
     prohibits *rebuilding what is still current*, not bounded cache management.
2. A partition whose **effective edit set** has not changed since the previous extract MUST NOT be
   invalidated on account of an edit.
3. Determining a partition's effective edit set MUST be bounded by a function of the edits intersecting that
   partition, and MUST be independent of the edit stack's length.
4. Determining which partitions an edit invalidates MUST be bounded by a function of that edit's own extent,
   and MUST NOT require re-evaluating the edit stack.
5. Conformance to (3) and (4) MUST be verified by measuring cost across edit stacks differing in length by at
   least an order of magnitude, with the number of intersecting edits held constant, and demonstrating that
   cost does not track stack length.

#### Rationale

(3) and (4) are stated as cost bounds rather than as mechanisms, because the mechanism is an implementation
choice and the bound is what a consumer can rely on. Both are satisfiable by indexing the edit stack
spatially and by scoping each edit's change signal to its own region, and that is the expected
implementation — but an obligation to *be spatially indexed* would specify how rather than what, and a
different structure meeting the same bounds would conform.

Together they are what make a long edit stack survivable. Without them, every partition read replays every
edit, and a day of manual correction makes a file progressively slower to open — the failure any naive edit
log has. With them, a partition intersects a handful of edits regardless of how many exist.

(1) inverts the usual engine arrangement deliberately, and the cost is real: retained state with incremental
invalidation is harder than clearing and rebuilding, and it is the only viable option here. Its nested
qualification exists because "MUST be retained" read literally would forbid eviction, which no clause
permits and every implementation needs.

(2) is stated negatively for the same reason. The positive form — only a changed partition *may* be
invalidated — prohibits invalidating for any non-edit reason, including a partition leaving the frustum.

(3) and (4) say **bounded by** rather than "cost a function of", because every cost is a function of
something, so the positive half of that phrasing carried no content and only the prohibitions did.

(5) supplies the verification every other scaling claim in this specification carries —
[RFC-0002:C-MEMORY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-memory) 5, [RFC-0002:C-HALO](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-halo) 4, [RFC-0002:C-PROJECTION](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-projection) 3. Without it, "MUST be
independent of the edit stack's length" is a claim no test is obliged to make, and this clause's whole
purpose is that a day of manual correction must not make a file slower to open.

### [RFC-0007:C-BAKE] Consolidation of the executable representation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-bake"></a>

Spatial indexing makes finding the relevant edits cheap, but not applying them: a heavily corrected stand
still accumulates deep chains over the same partitions. Consolidation is therefore required, and it happens
without being asked for.

1. The system MUST consolidate — **bake** — the executable representation of the edit stack without user
   action, when the cost of evaluating a region's effective edit set exceeds a configured threshold.
   - The threshold MUST be observable and reportable.
   - The measured cost, or the outcome of comparing it against the threshold, MUST also be observable.
2. Baking MUST NOT change the result of evaluating the document graph.
   - A baked and an unbaked evaluation of the same document MUST produce identical output.
3. Baking MUST affect only the executable representation.
   - It MUST NOT alter, collapse, reorder, or discard recorded history (C-PROVENANCE).
4. A baked representation MUST be re-derivable from recorded history alone, and MUST be discardable at any
   time without data loss.

#### Rationale

Transparent rather than user-invoked, because the alternative does not work in practice. An explicit "flatten
history" command is predictable and will not be run; the observable outcome is a workbench that grows slower
over a day's work and a user who has no reason to connect the two. Consolidation is a caching concern, and
caches that require manual invalidation are not caches.

The nested requirement in (1) is what turns a delegated value into a verifiable obligation. Delegating the
threshold is right — it depends on the machine — but an unobservable threshold makes "the system MUST
consolidate" unfalsifiable. Both halves are needed: an observable threshold with an unobservable measured
cost still leaves a test unable to establish the condition was met, which is the gap the first version of
this bullet left open. This mirrors the pattern [RFC-0003:C-COMMIT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-commit) 4 uses to make
[RFC-0003:C-COMMIT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-commit) 2 checkable.

(2) is what makes (1) safe to do unasked. If baking could change results, doing it automatically would mean
the system silently altering a forester's output on a threshold the forester cannot see.

(4) is the property that makes a baked representation a cache rather than a second source of truth. Because
it is re-derivable and discardable, a bake defect is recoverable by deletion, and a corrupted bake cannot
destroy work. It is also what [RFC-0004:C-CACHE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-cache) 1 generalises to every cache.

### [RFC-0007:C-PROVENANCE] Append-only edit history (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-provenance"></a>

A manual reclassification can change a timber volume estimate, and that estimate may be acted on
commercially. "Who changed what, and when" is therefore a question the system must answer about its own
output, not merely an undo convenience.

1. Recorded edit history MUST be append-only.
   - An undone or superseded edit MUST be retained as a recorded event rather than removed.
2. Every recorded edit MUST carry what is needed to re-derive its effect:
   - its region or its enumerated point set;
   - its predicate, where it has one;
   - its action;
   - its position in the order.
3. History MUST NOT be discarded by baking (C-BAKE 3), by cache eviction, or by any space-reclamation
   mechanism.
4. An output produced from an edited document MUST carry a reference to the recorded history that produced
   it, and that reference MUST resolve to a history whose recorded edits are those the output was evaluated
   from.
5. The document graph MUST be recordable in a serialised form that names each operator and its parameters,
   and from which the graph can be reconstructed.
   - That form MUST be the same representation used to record history under (1) to (4), not a parallel one.

#### Rationale

This is nearly free if designed in and impossible to add retroactively. The stack is already an ordered
sequence of small records (C-EDIT 2), so retaining superseded ones costs approximately nothing;
reconstructing a history that was never kept costs everything.

(1) is what separates history from undo state. Undo needs only the ability to reach the previous state;
provenance needs the record that the intermediate state existed and was rejected — frequently the interesting
part of an audit.

(3) names the mechanisms that would otherwise erode this by degrees. No individual eviction looks like
discarding an audit trail, which is exactly how audit trails get discarded.

(5) is what makes the graph a *document* rather than only a runtime structure, and it is required here rather
than elsewhere because history and graph are the same thing recorded at different granularity — an edit is a
node, so a format that can record the history can record the graph. Requiring one representation prevents the
familiar outcome where a pipeline format and a document format drift apart and disagree about semantics.
[RFC-0002:C-EXTENSION](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-extension) 2 depends on this item.
